name: Nielsen's 10 Usability Heuristics
description: Jakob Nielsen's 10 general principles for interaction design

categories.title: Visibility of System Status
categories.description: The design should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within a reasonable amount of time.
questions: Does the design show clear feedback for user actions?
Are loading states visible and informative?
Is the current page/state clearly indicated?
Are progress indicators present for long operations?
Do interactive elements show hover/active states?
checkpoints: Verify button states (default, hover, active, disabled)
Validate form field feedback (error, success, focus)

categories.title: Match Between System and Real World
categories.description: The design should speak the users' language, with words, phrases, and concepts familiar to the user.
questions: Does the interface use familiar terminology?
Are icons recognizable and intuitive?
Does information appear in a natural and logical order?
Are metaphors appropriate and consistent?
checkpoints: Review all labels and button text

categories.title: User Control and Freedom
categories.description: Users often perform actions by mistake. They need a clearly marked 'emergency exit' to leave the unwanted action.
questions: Can users easily undo actions?
Are there clear exit points from flows?
Can users cancel operations in progress?
Is there a way to go back to previous states?

categories.title: Consistency and Standards
categories.description: Users should not have to wonder whether different words, situations, or actions mean the same thing.
questions: Are similar elements styled consistently?
Do buttons follow the same patterns throughout?
Is terminology consistent across the interface?
Are interaction patterns predictable?

categories.title: Error Prevention
categories.description: Good error messages are important, but the best designs carefully prevent problems from occurring in the first place.
questions: Are destructive actions confirmed?
Do forms validate input before submission?
Are constraints clearly communicated?
Are dangerous actions protected?
checkpoints: Check for confirmation dialogs on delete actions
Test disabled states prevent invalid actions

categories.title: Recognition Rather Than Recall
categories.description: Minimize the user's memory load by making elements, actions, and options visible.
questions: Are options and actions visible?
Is context provided where needed?
Are instructions available when necessary?
Do tooltips explain complex features?
checkpoints: Verify tooltips on icons and complex controls
Confirm dropdown menus show all options

categories.title: Flexibility and Efficiency of Use
categories.description: Shortcuts—hidden from novice users—may speed up the interaction for the expert user.
questions: Are there keyboard shortcuts for common actions?
Can power users customize their experience?
Are there quick actions for frequent tasks?
Do advanced features exist without cluttering the interface?

categories.title: Aesthetic and Minimalist Design
categories.description: Interfaces should not contain information which is irrelevant or rarely needed.
questions: Is the visual design clean and uncluttered?
Does every element serve a purpose?
Is the information hierarchy clear?
Are distractions minimized?

categories.title: Help Users Recognize, Diagnose, and Recover from Errors
categories.description: Error messages should be expressed in plain language, precisely indicate the problem, and constructively suggest a solution.
questions: Are error messages clear and helpful?
Do errors explain what went wrong?
Are solutions suggested?
Is the error message tone appropriate?
checkpoints: Verify errors are specific, not generic

categories.title: Help and Documentation
categories.description: It's best if the system doesn't need any additional explanation. However, it may be necessary to provide documentation.
questions: Is help easily accessible?
Is documentation searchable?
Are examples provided?
Is onboarding available for new users?
checkpoints: Check for help links or buttons
